accepted.s: The proposal for constructing an anicut near Rajahmundry was urged by Arthur Cotton before the Board of Revenue in which year?
accepted.x: Arthur Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue in 1844, urging the construction of an anicut near Rajahmundry.
accepted.tq: Test the precise year associated with the administrative proposal.
accepted.sec: Anicuts - Dowleswaram, Vijayawada, Sangam; Cotton, Veeranna, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.x: The Dowleswaram anicut was sanctioned in late 1846; its construction began in 1847.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dowleswaram anicut:
1. Its main work was completed in April 1852.
2. Its reported cost was Rs 1.5 lakh.
3. Veenam Veeranna served as an Indian assistant in the project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The main work was completed in April 1852 at a cost of Rs 1.5 lakh, with Veenam Veeranna serving as Indian assistant.
accepted.tq: Combine completion date, cost and personnel facts in a statement set.
accepted.sec: Anicuts - Dowleswaram, Vijayawada, Sangam; Cotton, Veeranna, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.s: Veenam Veeranna, associated with the construction of the Dowleswaram anicut, was made:
accepted.x: Veenam Veeranna was made Rao Bahadur and served as an Assistant Engineer in connection with the project.
accepted.tq: Test the exact designation and honour attached to a named individual.
accepted.sec: Anicuts - Dowleswaram, Vijayawada, Sangam; Cotton, Veeranna, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was constructed during 1852–55, not in 1872. The K.C. Canal dates to 1872, while Dowleswaram was begun in 1847 and the Penna anicut dates to 1860.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Godavari irrigation system mentioned in connection with the anicuts?
o: It consisted of two canals and initially irrigated 1.5 lakh acres.
It consisted of three main canals and initially irrigated 6.62 lakh acres.
It consisted of three canals and initially irrigated 10 lakh acres only.
It consisted of six canals and initially irrigated 3.26 lakh acres.
accepted.x: The Godavari system had three main canals and covered 6.62 lakh acres initially; the area later rose to 10 lakh acres.
accepted.tq: Separate the initial figure from the later expanded figure.
accepted.sec: Anicuts - Dowleswaram, Vijayawada, Sangam; Cotton, Veeranna, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.s: The revenue from the Godavari irrigation system increased from Rs 20.38 lakh in 1853–54 to approximately:
accepted.x: The revenue increased from Rs 20.38 lakh in 1853–54 to Rs 55.18 lakh in 1894–95.
accepted.tq: Match both endpoints of a quantitative trend rather than one isolated number.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a major feature of the economic impact of British rule on handicrafts in Andhra?
o: Handicrafts were protected by complete prohibition of imported goods.
Artisans received increased traditional patronage from local courts.
British manufactured goods entered the market duty-free and artisans lost patronage.
Artisans were shifted exclusively to government employment.
accepted.x: Deindustrialisation occurred because artisans lost traditional patronage and British goods entered duty-free.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct cause-effect explanation for deindustrialisation.
accepted.sec: Economic impact - handicrafts, commercial crops, land revenue burden

accepted.s: Why did the cash revenue demand encourage farmers to shift towards commercial crops?
o: Food crops were exempt from revenue, so farmers abandoned all commercial crops.
Farmers received fixed cash subsidies for growing only cotton.
Revenue had to be paid in cash, encouraging cultivation of tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds.
The government prohibited the cultivation of rice throughout Andhra.
accepted.x: Since land revenue had to be paid in cash, farmers increasingly cultivated commercial crops such as tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds.
accepted.tq: Apply the cash-revenue mechanism to the observed change in cropping pattern.
accepted.sec: Economic impact - handicrafts, commercial crops, land revenue burden

accepted.s: The reduction of land under food crops made the region more:
accepted.x: The shift from food crops to commercial crops reduced food availability and made the region more vulnerable to famines.
accepted.tq: Follow the chain from commercialisation to food insecurity and famine vulnerability.
accepted.sec: Economic impact - handicrafts, commercial crops, land revenue burden

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about agriculture in Andhra under British rule:
1. Most people depended on agriculture.
2. Rice was the main crop.
3. Commercial crops completely replaced food crops in all districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Most people depended on agriculture and rice was the main crop. Commercial crops did not completely replace food crops in all districts.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the two supported agricultural facts.
accepted.sec: Economic impact - handicrafts, commercial crops, land revenue burden

accepted.s: The principal role of the railways that reached Andhra in the late nineteenth century was to:
o: Link the interior with the Madras port
Link Andhra exclusively with Bombay port
Connect only the Agency tracts with Calcutta
accepted.x: The railways linked the interior of Andhra with the port of Madras, facilitating movement and trade.
accepted.tq: Test the direction and commercial purpose of an early transport link.

accepted.s: During the British period, Vizagapatnam port began developing particularly for the export of:
accepted.x: Vizagapatnam port developed for the movement of iron ore and agricultural exports.
accepted.tq: Match a port with its stated export commodities.

accepted.s: The Buckingham Canal is best described as a:
o: Feeder canal exclusively for the K.C. Canal
Freshwater irrigation canal linking the Krishna and Godavari
Mountain canal connecting Andhra with Mysore
Salt-water navigation canal running along the coast through Pulicat Lake
accepted.x: The Buckingham Canal was a salt-water navigation canal along the coast, passing through Pulicat Lake.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a navigation canal from irrigation and feeder canals.
accepted.sec: Railways, roads, telegraph and canals - first lines, Buckingham Canal

accepted.s: The Buckingham Canal forms part of which National Waterway, along with the Eluru and Kakinada canals?
accepted.x: The Buckingham Canal is now part of NW-4, the Kakinada–Puducherry waterway, along with the Eluru and Kakinada canals.
accepted.tq: Test the canal–national waterway association directly.
accepted.sec: Railways, roads, telegraph and canals - first lines, Buckingham Canal

accepted.s: The Buckingham Canal was extended as a famine-relief measure during:
accepted.x: The Buckingham Canal was extended as famine relief during 1876–78.

accepted.s: Which famine affected the Northern Circars during 1790–92, with the Ganjam famine occurring in 1791–92?
accepted.x: The Northern Circars famine occurred during 1790–92, and the Ganjam famine formed part of the 1791–92 crisis.
accepted.tq: Match a famine label with its period and regional setting.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.s: The famine affecting all Andhra districts during 1805–07 was followed by a famine in 1823 affecting several districts, including:
o: Kadapa, Kurnool, Chittoor, Guntur, Vizag and Nellore
accepted.x: The 1823 famine affected Kadapa, Kurnool, Chittoor, Guntur, Vizag and Nellore; the 1805–07 famine affected all Andhra districts.
accepted.tq: Use the complete regional list to distinguish the 1823 famine from other entries.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Guntur famine of 1832–33 is correct?
o: It was confined to Kurnool and caused 40 per cent deaths.
It affected only the Northern Circars and caused no migration.
It occurred after the American Civil War and centred on cotton.
It was the worst famine in the south and caused about two lakh deaths.
accepted.x: The Guntur famine of 1832–33 was regarded as the worst in the south and caused about two lakh deaths, though one account gives the death share as 40 per cent.
accepted.tq: Identify the famine with its severity, deaths and regional description.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Kurnool famine occurred in 1866. The other pairs assign incorrect dates to the named famines.
accepted.tq: Check famine names against their exact years rather than relying on regional familiarity.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.s: Budda Vengala Reddy is associated with relief during the Kurnool famine of 1866. He was awarded a gold medal on:
accepted.x: Budda Vengala Reddy fed people during the 1866 Kurnool famine and received a gold medal on 1 January 1877.
accepted.tq: Link a relief figure, famine and award date in one precise recall question.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.s: The Ganjam famine after 1865 was closely connected with:
o: The end of American Civil War cotton demand and migration to Mauritius and Sri Lanka
The opening of the Madras port and migration to Burma only
The construction of the K.C. Canal and migration to Mysore
The introduction of ryotwari and migration to Bengal
accepted.x: The decline in cotton demand after the American Civil War contributed to the Ganjam famine, after which people migrated to Mauritius and Sri Lanka.
accepted.tq: Connect an international economic change with regional famine and migration.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.tq: Match a major famine with its presidency-level region.

accepted.s: Which statement about famines in the late nineteenth century is correct?
o: There were no major famines after 1852.
There were eleven famines, all confined to Ganjam.
There were eleven famines, and 1865–66 was the most severe.
There were three famines, and 1832–33 was the only severe one.
accepted.x: The late nineteenth century witnessed eleven famines, with 1865–66 described as the most severe.
accepted.tq: Test both the count and the comparative severity of famines.
accepted.sec: Famines under British rule - year and region

accepted.s: After Crown rule, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts in:
accepted.x: In 1859, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts respectively.
accepted.tq: Test the chronology of district renaming and reorganisation.
accepted.sec: Madras Presidency districts of Andhra - reorganisation

accepted.s:
Arrange the following district developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of West Godavari district
B. Union of Rajahmundry and Kakinada collectorates
C. Reorganisation into Godavari and Krishna districts
D. Formation of Guntur and East Godavari districts
accepted.x: The correct order is 1802, 1859, 1904 and 1925: union of collectorates, reorganisation into Godavari and Krishna, formation of Guntur and East Godavari, and formation of West Godavari.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two middle reorganisation stages.
accepted.sec: Madras Presidency districts of Andhra - reorganisation

accepted.s: Guntur and East Godavari became districts in 1904, while West Godavari became a district in:
accepted.x: Guntur and East Godavari became districts in 1904, and West Godavari was formed in 1925.
accepted.tq: Compare two related district-formation dates.
accepted.sec: Madras Presidency districts of Andhra - reorganisation

accepted.s: The Collector in the Madras Presidency combined which set of powers?
o: Legislative, judicial and diplomatic powers only
accepted.x: The Collector combined revenue, magisterial and police powers.
